$comment: Consumers of the canonical Snyk policy in snyk-policy/base.snyk.
Steady state: a repo's .snyk is [canonical block][# repo-specific][tail].
The sync regenerates the block and preserves the tail byte-for-byte, so a
repo only appears here to (a) opt in, (b) carry a note rendered into the
block, or (c) declare a ONE-TIME migration for a file that predates the
migrate.tail — how to derive the tail the first time a repo is converted:
"none"            the whole existing file is canonical-shaped; drop it
{ "from": "..." } tail starts at the first line containing this string
Once the marker is in place the directive is inert and can be deleted.
migrate: "manual" excludes a repo from automated conversion entirely. It
is still checked, and reported, but never rewritten.
Adding a repo: add a key here. The sync creates .snyk if it is absent.

reviewers.$why: Its licence list IS the canonical block; the marker sat above it.

nswds-email.$why: Same as reviewers — licence list moves into the canonical block.

attestation.$why: Base + licence list only; no policy of its own.

nswds-ui.$why: Carried only the two obsolete nanoid ignores. Note: the Snyk Code exclude that docs/config-single-source-of-truth.md attributes to this repo now lives in nswds-email-framework.

awards.$why: Tail was only the dead '*:lic:*' catch-all, which the enumerated licence list replaces.

tail.from: # ── repo-specific: generated output is not scanned

nswds-email-framework.$why: Keeps its top-level `exclude:` block for generated docs/ and build_local/.

nswds-tokens.$why: Keeps its javascript/PT Snyk Code ignore; drops the dead catch-all above it.

nswds-app.$why: Keeps its two transitive postcss ignores; drops the dead catch-all above them.

dtl-sandbox.$why: Its path-scoping rationale is top-of-file prose above `ignore:`, which the canonical block now owns. Re-homing that prose into the tail is a judgement call, not a mechanical move — convert it by hand, then delete this directive.
